title: First survey
note: Photographed both front beds. Bed 1 still in heavy bloom and badly under-deadheaded. Bed 2 mostly finished and full of ripe poppy seed. Two plants unidentified, gladiolus showing possible thrips damage, one stalk with a long vertical split.

title: Questions answered
note: The woolly spikes are snapdragons, no lupines in either bed. Split stem closed, nothing obvious on the ground. Gladiolus already overwinter in these beds and get lifted and spread each fall, so the corm question is settled: keep the existing routine and add a corm inspection while they are up. Still open: whether the whorled spike plant is veronica or agastache.
